fields.reason: ATO Corporate Tax Transparency publishes the entity's registered name, and all held-out values are registered-style legal names (PTY LTD / PTY LIMITED). No trading-name or contact-person source column exists, so legal_name is the correct target.

Column 'ABN' contains 11-digit values and the abn transform applies checksum validation; emitted values are 11 digits and the claim is typed as entity.abn. No ACN-style 9-digit or NZBN 13-digit values appear in the held-out rows.

Constant AU for address.country is supported: the publisher is the ATO and the record identity is an ABN, which is uniquely Australian. This is a jurisdiction-level default, not a premises address claim, so it is acceptable as a country constant.

critic.summary: All three rules are sound. Name->legal_name is justified because the ATO transparency dataset publishes registered entity names, and the held-out records show only registered-style suffixes, not trading or contact names. ABN mapping uses checksum validation appropriate to the ontology requirement. The AU country constant is a jurisdiction default rather than a site address, which the ontology permits as a default. The unmapped monetary columns and income-year label genuinely have no ontology target (Income year is a reporting period for entity-year facts, not a validity date for the name or registration), so no missed mappings are identified. No validity_date or status claims are emitted, so the usual failure modes around date attachment, legacy record-level validity, and deregistered valid_to do not apply here.

fields.reason: ATO Corporate Tax Transparency publishes the registered entity name for the ABN holder; values are registered-style legal names (PTY LTD / PTY LIMITED / LIMITED). Not a trading name, not a contact person's name. claim_scope 'current_legal_name' is consistent — no validity date is attached, so no date-misattribution risk. Whitespace normalisation only.

Source column is literally 'ABN'; values are 11 digits and the abn transform applies the ABN checksum rather than a bare length check, matching the ontology note. Emitted value is 11 digits, consistent with ^\d{11}$.

Constant country AU is justified: the publisher is the ATO and every record is identified by an Australian Business Number, so records are Australian entities. This is a country-level assertion only — it does not claim a street/postal/premises address, so no address-type confusion.

missed.reason: Legal-name suffixes (PTY LTD, PTY LIMITED, LIMITED, HOLDINGS, HOLDCO) are explicit in-source evidence that lets entity_type be set to 'company' (and 'unknown' otherwise) rather than left unmapped; the ontology warns specifically against guessing entity_type, so this precise source signal should be captured or the field explicitly justified as unknown.

critic.summary: All three rules are defensible: legal_name sourced from the ATO registered name column, ABN validated with a checksum transform, and a country constant warranted by the ATO/ABN context. No validity dates are emitted, so no date-order or licence-date-on-name misattribution, no legacy record-level validity target, and no status is asserted (so no deregistered/valid_to conflict). Financial amounts and the income year are correctly left unmapped. Main gap: entity_type is derivable with fair confidence from explicit legal-name suffixes in the same source column and was not captured; if it stays unmapped it should be recorded as 'unknown' by default rather than inferred elsewhere.
